claim_being_audited: Whether certifying the current model release is policy-compliant and evidentially supported despite a current seller-enforcement subgroup regression, based on aggregate readiness evidence plus disclosure of the limitation.
decision_criteria: Compliant certification requires current release documentation reflecting current evaluation results.
Material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless covered by approved mitigation.
Aggregate pass and clean rehearsal are supportive but do not override a missing disclosure or mitigation predicate.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring may be contextual support only, not substitutes for current evidence.
evidence_requests: Produce the current release model card or certification packet showing the present eval batch results are reflected.
Produce the exact disclosure text covering the seller-enforcement subgroup weakness in current release documentation.
Produce evidence that the seller-enforcement weakness was assessed as non-material for the named launch use case, if that is the position.
If disclosure is incomplete, produce the approved mitigation or formal risk-acceptance record that covers this release-specific weakness.
Produce the underlying current evaluation results for the seller-enforcement slice and the aggregate threshold calculation.
specific_concerns: The admissible record, as summarized, supports aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, but it also identifies a current seller-enforcement weakness for a named launch slice.
Policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses, or else show approved mitigation/risk acceptance.
No admissible evidence is provided that the current model card/documentation has in fact been updated for this release.
No admissible evidence is provided of an approved mitigation or risk acceptance covering the current seller-enforcement regression.
Prior approval of the same model family and informal monitoring are explicitly contextual only under the policy and cannot close the current-release support gap.
unsupported_claims: That certification may proceed now, rather than only conditionally, is not fully supported because the required current-release documentation or approved mitigation is not evidenced.
Any implication that prior approval materially supports current compliance beyond context is unsupported under the stated policy.
Any implication that disclosure has already occurred is unsupported by the available actor-summary-only record.
